notes: Summary: Enterprise fintech product team exploring LLM layer for agent support + document ranking. Wanted fast time-to-value and low integration overhead.
Initial contact (2025-09): inbound from engineering lead after seeing benchmark blog. Very interested in cost controls + model routing but priority = speed to production.
POC agreed (Oct 2025): 6-week sandbox to prove chat + rerank. Redwood proposed hosted_api + Optimize recommendations for batching.
Security review (Nov 2025): asked for SOC2 report, SSO options. Provided SOC2 attestation and security FAQ (drive link). Halcyon asked about data residency for EU customers.
Technical POC notes (Dec 2025): good latency in our hosted env. SE Carlos ran perf tests: median 2xxms for 256-token chat in east-us; product liked consistent percentiles.
Sales thread (Dec): pricing tension. Halcyon lean on unit economics; wanted a single per-token model billing with simple forecasting. They flagged procurement inertia vs. direct vendor APIs.
Competitive move (Jan 2026): procurement informed team signed a short-term contract with OpenAI direct API. Reason cited: 'simpler integration, brand trust, fewer meetings' (quote from Head of Eng).

Call 2026-01-08 (FF-2026-01-08-halcyon-demo): Maya + Carlos demoed rollout patterns and routing/fallback. Customer appreciated canary/A-B features but said they'd defer to direct provider to move faster.
Internal notes: no clear internal champion after Head of ML left in Dec; replacement hiring on hold → procurement unwilling to commit to enterprise contract.
Action items before close: offered 90-day proof extension, special pilot pricing, and a small concierge onboarding. All declined — cited vendor simplification and existing credit with OpenAI.

Decision: Closed-lost (competed against OpenAI/Anthropic). Primary reasons logged: simplicity of direct APIs, existing internal preference for major brand, and hiring/budget freeze. Low security blocker impact — SOC2 answers were fine.
Next recommended cadence: re-engage if the hiring freeze ends or if they hit cost/latency pain in 3–6 months. Tag account for marketing drip on model routing and cost comparison case studies.
Quoted: 'We want to keep this low-friction — right now a hosted direct vendor gives us the path of least resistance.' — Head of Engineering (paraphrased)
Jira: INF-4122 created for follow-up on POC infra notes; resolved when POC archived.
Attachments: proposal v2, security answers spreadsheet, demo recording metadata in Fireflies.
Sales notes style: short bullets, kept threads; push for re-open if they show MRR growth or expand to EU residency needs.
